**New Evidence**
- Appointments and delegation are now better evidenced at the fiscal center.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Intervención inicial del secretario de Hacienda y Crédito Público, Rogelio Ramírez de la O, durante su comparecencia en Sesión Ordinaria del Senado, como parte de la Glosa del Cuarto Informe de Gobierno","publisher":"Coordinación de Comunicación Social del Senado de la República","publication_date":"2022-09-28","url":"https://comunicacionsocial.senado.gob.mx/informacion/prensa/3784-intervencion-inicial-del-secretario-de-hacienda-y-credito-publico-rogelio-ramirez-de-la-o-durante-su-comparecencia-en-sesion-ordinaria-del-senado-como-parte-de-la-glosa-del-cuarto-informe-de-gobierno","claim":"Ramírez de la O appeared before the Senate under oath to report on the 2022 fiscal package and macroeconomic policy, showing a real delegated implementation channel for AMLO's program.","locator":"opening paragraph and oath section","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary legislative transcript for a named cabinet official and the target-year budget process; strong for delegation and oversight, not for performance quality.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022.","ruler_attribution":"High attribution: Ramírez de la O was AMLO's finance secretary and the central fiscal operator, though outcomes still reflect external shocks and congressional constraints.","contrary_evidence":["This confirms process and authority, not successful execution by itself."],"lenses":["8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5"]}
- A second appointment shows executive selection of a technically capable spending official.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Comunicado No. 9 Juan Pablo de Botton fue ratificado por la Cámara de Diputados como subsecretario de Egresos","publisher":"Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público","publication_date":"2022-02-01","url":"https://www.gob.mx/shcp/prensa/comunicado-no-9-juan-pablo-de-botton-fue-ratificado-por-la-camara-de-diputados-como-subsecretario-de-egresos?idiom=es-MX","claim":"Juan Pablo de Botton was ratified as subsecretary of Egresos, with an explicit mandate to make spending effective, efficient, transparent, and fiscally responsible.","locator":"first paragraphs and the mandate description","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official appointment notice with clear role description and policy mandate; strong for personnel selection, not for downstream results.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to the AMLO administration's staffing choices, though one appointment does not prove broad competence.","contrary_evidence":["This is appointment evidence, not proof of the quality of execution across the whole administration."],"lenses":["8B.2","8B.4","8B.5"]}
- IMSS-Bienestar moved from rhetoric into an actual state-federal transition.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Autoridades federales y de Colima inician transición del sistema de salud estatal a IMSS-Bienestar","publisher":"Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social","publication_date":"2022-05-18","url":"https://www.imss.gob.mx/prensa/archivo/202205/CC009","claim":"Federal and Colima authorities signed a transition table to implement and operate IMSS-Bienestar, with diagnostics for staffing, infrastructure, and medicine supply, and Zoé Robledo said it was advancing on AMLO's instruction.","locator":"opening paragraphs and the diagnostics section","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary implementation notice with concrete state transition steps and operational details; strong evidence of execution, though still partial and state-specific.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022.","ruler_attribution":"High attribution for policy direction; implementation was carried by health officials and a state governor, so this is delegation-plus-execution evidence rather than personal micromanagement.","contrary_evidence":["This shows implementation in one state and a transition process, not complete national rollout or service-quality proof."],"lenses":["8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"]}
- The health federalization program was formalized as a binding government instrument.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"ACUERDO por el que se emite el Programa Estratégico de Salud para el Bienestar","publisher":"Diario Oficial de la Federación / Secretaría de Salud","publication_date":"2022-09-07","url":"https://dof.gob.mx/nota_detalle.php?codigo=5663700&fecha=07/09/2022","claim":"The federal government issued a mandatory strategic health program that defined the objectives, strategies, and actions for federalizing and progressively extending free health services to people without social security.","locator":"article one and the explanatory recitals","source_type":"primary/legal","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Formal legal act in the target year; very strong evidence for operationalization and institutionalization, weaker for realized service quality.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to the AMLO government, although the decree itself is not proof of successful delivery on the ground.","contrary_evidence":["A decree does not itself show nationwide implementation quality or durability."],"lenses":["8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"]}
- The main welfare-outcome improvement is only partly attributable to AMLO because external labor demand mattered materially.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Mexico Overview: Development news, research, data","publisher":"World Bank","publication_date":"2025","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/mexico/overview","claim":"The World Bank says Mexico's official multidimensional poverty rate fell to 36.3 percent in 2022 and that the gain was driven mainly by labor market outcomes, including increases in the minimum wage.","locator":"poverty paragraph in the overview page","source_type":"IGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Independent World Bank summary that explicitly links the 2022 poverty decline to labor-market drivers; retrospective but directly on point.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Retrospective evidence about the 2022 outcome window.","ruler_attribution":"Partial attribution only: minimum wage policy is AMLO-linked, but the World Bank says labor-market outcomes were the main driver rather than a single ruler-controlled program.","contrary_evidence":["The same framing reduces the case for claiming full AMLO ownership of the 2022 poverty decline."],"lenses":["8B.7","8B.10"]}
- External conditions clearly boosted household income through remittances.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Remittances Grow 5% in 2022, Despite Global Headwinds","publisher":"World Bank","publication_date":"2022-11-30","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2022/11/30/remittances-grow-5-percent-2022","claim":"The World Bank reported that remittances to Mexico rose 12.9 percent to 61.1 billion dollars in 2022, aided by the strong U.S. labor market.","locator":"Latin America and the Caribbean paragraph","source_type":"IGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Authoritative external data note with a direct Mexico-specific 2022 remittance figure and driver; strong for external attribution.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within 2022.","ruler_attribution":"This is mostly external, not ruler-driven; it matters because it weakens any claim that 2022 household gains were solely due to AMLO policy.","contrary_evidence":["Remittance gains do not by themselves prove domestic policy competence."],"lenses":["8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"]}

**Gap Status**
- Appointments and delegation: partly resolved. The fiscal and spending core now has explicit 2022 appointment evidence, but I still do not have a complete cabinet-wide delegation map.
- Program-to-implementation: partly resolved. IMSS-Bienestar and the health-program decree show real operationalization, not just slogans.
- Regulatory predictability and anti-capture: partly resolved in the negative direction. The current record still supports uncertainty around energy and investment rules, but I did not find a cleaner 2022 sectoral implementation audit in this round.
- Outcome attribution: partly resolved. The 2022 poverty improvement is better grounded now, but the exact AMLO share is not recoverable from current evidence because labor-market conditions and remittances materially contributed.
- Exact causal decomposition: not recoverable in this round.

**Search and Rejection Summary**
- I checked about a dozen additional documents in this follow-up, mainly SHCP, Senate, IMSS, DOF, World Bank, OECD, IMF, and CONEVAL items.
- I kept only the sources that changed the gap picture: executive appointments, health federalization, and external attribution for the 2022 poverty decline.
- I rejected duplicate mirrors of the same official statements, plus broader macro context that was already covered in the current index and did not add a new AMLO-specific implementation link.
- I did not find a better direct audit of the full 2022 delegation chain or a more precise decomposition of the 2022 poverty decline than the sources already cited here.
